topic_ko: 우리는 수동적 관찰자가 아니라 변화를 일으키는 존재
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 31번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외.

passage: Our world is not merely interconnected; it is constantly changing, even when we fail to notice it.
While you read these words, you yourself are changing, aging just a little and reshaping the neural networks in your brain.
Even when you seem to be doing nothing important, distant events are quietly unfolding that will alter your life later on.
The ancient Greek philosopher Heraclitus put it well: no one ever steps into the same river twice, for neither the river nor the person stays the same.
His student Cratylus pushed the idea further, insisting that we are not simply onlookers watching the flow.
When we step into the river, we stir it and reshape it, so we are agents who help make the change happen.
choices: why ancient Greek philosophers disagreed about the nature of rivers
that we are not passive observers but active agents of constant change
how the human brain forms new neural networks during reading
why distant events rarely have any real effect on our daily lives
how aging gradually slows down the way people perceive the world
theme.explanation_ko: 세계도 우리도 끊임없이 변하며, 강에 발을 들이는 순간 우리가 강을 바꾸므로 우리는 단순한 관찰자가 아니라 변화를 일으키는 존재라는 내용. ②가 주제로 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①철학자들의 견해 차이, ③뇌 신경망 형성, ④원거리 사건의 무관함, ⑤노화와 지각 속도는 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should not picture ourselves as detached spectators standing safely outside the flow of the world.
Everything is interconnected and ceaselessly changing, even when our senses miss the movement entirely.
As you read, your body ages slightly and your brain quietly rewires itself with every word.
Heraclitus reminded us that no one steps into the same river twice, since both the river and the person have changed.
Cratylus added that we are far more than passive observers of this endless flow.
Because the moment we enter the river we disturb and alter it, we should see ourselves as participants who shape the change around us.
choices: 고대 철학자들의 말은 오늘날에는 더 이상 받아들일 필요가 없다.
세상의 변화를 막기 위해 우리는 가능한 한 행동을 자제해야 한다.
우리는 변화의 흐름 밖에서 지켜보는 구경꾼이 아니라 변화를 만드는 참여자로 자신을 보아야 한다.
뇌의 신경망은 독서를 통해서만 새롭게 형성될 수 있다.
강은 사람보다 훨씬 빠르게 변하므로 늘 주의해서 다뤄야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 강에 들어서는 순간 우리가 강을 바꾸므로 단순 관찰자가 아니라 변화를 만드는 참여자로 자신을 보아야 한다는 주장. ③이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 본문의 핵심 주장과 무관하거나 지엽적이다.

passage: The world around us is woven together and never stops shifting, even though we usually cannot feel the motion.
Right now, as you read, you are aging a little and your brain's neural networks are silently changing.
Even in quiet moments, faraway events are already shaping the future course of your life.
Heraclitus observed that no person steps into the same river twice, for neither stays the same.
Cratylus went on to claim that we never merely stand by and watch the current pass.
Stepping in, we disturb the water itself, which means we are agents of change, not bystanders.
choices: 강물은 사람이 발을 들여도 본래의 흐름을 그대로 유지한다.
우리는 세상의 흐름을 지켜보기만 하는 관찰자가 아니라 변화를 일으키는 존재이다.
철학을 이해하려면 먼저 고대 그리스어를 배워야 한다.
노화는 독서를 통해 어느 정도 늦출 수 있다.
원거리에서 일어나는 사건은 개인의 삶과 거의 관련이 없다.
gist.explanation_ko: 세계도 우리도 끊임없이 변하고, 강에 들어서는 순간 우리가 강을 바꾸므로 우리는 관찰자가 아니라 변화를 일으키는 존재라는 것이 요지. ②가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①강물 불변, ③고대어 학습, ④노화 지연, ⑤원거리 사건의 무관함은 요지가 아니다.

passage: Beneath its surface, our world is endlessly interconnected and endlessly changing, whether or not we sense it.
Even while you read this sentence, you are aging slightly and your neural networks are quietly rearranging.
Far from your sight, events are taking shape that will one day reshape your own life.
Heraclitus famously said that no one steps into the same river twice, for the river and the person both change.
Cratylus carried the thought further: we are never just passive observers of the stream.
The instant we step in, we stir the water and become part of the change ourselves.
choices: Heraclitus and the Hidden History of Greek Rivers
Stepping In: Why We Shape the Change We Watch
How to Slow Down Aging While You Read
Why Distant Events Cannot Touch Our Lives
title.explanation_ko: 강에 발을 들이는 순간 우리가 변화를 만든다는 핵심을 압축한 ②가 제목으로 정답.
title.distractor_ko: ①강의 역사, ③노화 지연, ④뇌 신경망 설명, ⑤원거리 사건 무관함은 초점이 아니다.

passage: The world is not only interconnected but forever in motion, even when the motion escapes our notice.
As you read, you age a little and your brain rewires itself word by word.
Out of sight, events are already unfolding that will quietly change your future.
Heraclitus said no one steps into the same river twice, since neither the river nor the person remains unchanged.
Cratylus replied that we are not mere passive observers of the flow.
When we wade in, we ourselves trouble the water, so the river we touch is never left as we found it.
implication.underlined: the river we touch is never left as we found it
choices: rivers are too dangerous for people to enter without proper care
the past can never be recovered once a moment has gone by
our very presence alters the world we step into rather than leaving it unchanged
people should avoid disturbing nature whenever they possibly can
watching the world closely is the best way to understand it
implication.explanation_ko: '우리가 닿은 강은 결코 발견했을 때 그대로 남지 않는다'는 우리의 존재 자체가 우리가 들어선 세계를 바꾸어 놓는다는 뜻이다. ③이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①강의 위험, ②과거 회복 불가, ④자연 보호 권고, ⑤관찰의 중요성은 밑줄의 의미와 다르다.

passage: Our world is not just interconnected but ever-changing, even if we cannot sense it.
While you are reading this, the neural networks in your brain are imperceptible changing.
Even when we seem to do nothing of note, distant events are taking place that will change our lives later.
Heraclitus, the ancient Greek philosopher, rightly pointed out that no one steps into the same river twice.
Cratylus, a student of Heraclitus, added that we are not mere passive observers of the flow.
The moment we step into the river, we stir it, so we are agents who help make the change happen.
grammar.explanation_ko: ② 진행형 동사 changing을 수식하는 자리이므로 형용사 'imperceptible'이 아니라 부사 'imperceptibly'가 와야 한다. 'are imperceptibly changing'이 옳다. ②가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①형용사 ever-changing, ③events를 수식하는 주격 관계절 that will change, ④복수명사 observers, ⑤관계대명사 who의 정동사 help make는 모두 옳다.

passage: Our world is not just interconnected but ever-changing, even if we cannot sense it.
While you are reading this, the neural networks in your brain are imperceptibly shifting.
Even when we seem idle, distant events are unfolding that will preserve our lives in the future.
Heraclitus rightly noted that no one steps into the same river twice, for neither stays the same.
Cratylus added that we are not mere passive observers of the endless flow.
The instant we step into the river, we stir it, so we are agents who help make the change happen.
vocab.explanation_ko: ③ 먼 곳의 사건이 우리 삶을 바꾸어 놓는다는 문맥이므로 '그대로 보존하다(preserve)'가 아니라 '다시 빚다(reshape)'가 와야 한다. reshape로 고쳐야 한다. ③이 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①ever-changing(끊임없이 변하는), ②imperceptibly(감지할 수 없게), ④passive(수동적인), ⑤agents(행위 주체)는 문맥에 적절하다.

blank.explanation_ko: 강에 발을 들이는 순간 우리가 강을 바꾸므로, 우리는 단지 흐름을 지켜보는 '수동적 관찰자(passive observers)'가 아니다. ②가 정답.

irrelevant.intro: Our world is not only interconnected but ever-changing, even when we cannot sense the change.
sentences: While you are reading these words, you are aging just a little and your brain's neural networks are imperceptibly changing.
Even when we seem to be doing nothing important, distant events are taking place that will reshape our lives later on.
Heraclitus rightly observed that no one steps into the same river twice, for neither the river nor the person stays the same.
Geologists can estimate the age of a riverbed by studying the layers of sediment deposited along its banks.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '세계도 우리도 끊임없이 변하며 우리는 변화를 일으키는 존재'라는 흐름인데 ④ '지질학자가 퇴적층으로 강바닥 연대를 추정한다'는 무관한 내용이다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②③⑤는 모두 변화와 우리의 능동적 역할이라는 주제로 연결된다.

order.given: Our world is not just interconnected but ever-changing, even if we can't sense it, for while you read this, you are quietly changing too.

blocks.A: Heraclitus, the ancient Greek philosopher, rightly pointed out that no one ever steps into the same river twice, since neither the river nor the person remains the same.
blocks.B: You are aging a tiny amount, and the neural networks in your brain are imperceptibly changing as you take in each word.
blocks.C: To that, his student Cratylus added that we are not mere passive observers, because the moment we step in, we stir the water and shape the change ourselves.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '너도 변하고 있다'를 (B)가 노화·신경망으로 구체화, (A)가 Heraclitus의 강 비유로 일반화, (C)가 Cratylus로 마무리한다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (B)는 주어진 글의 'you are changing'을 곧장 잇고, (C)의 Cratylus는 'To that(Heraclitus의 말에)'를 받으므로 (A) 뒤라야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: To that, Cratylus, a student of Heraclitus, added that we are not mere passive observers of the flow.

passage_marked.text: Our world is not just interconnected but ever-changing, even if we cannot sense it.
While you are reading this, you are aging slightly and your brain's neural networks are imperceptibly changing.
Heraclitus, the ancient Greek philosopher, rightly pointed out that no one ever steps into the same river twice.
He meant that neither the river nor the person ever stays exactly the same.
After all, the moment we step in, we stir the water and become part of the change ourselves.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 'To that'은 바로 앞 Heraclitus의 강 비유 설명을 받고, Cratylus의 '수동적 관찰자가 아니다'라는 주장은 그 뒤의 'After all ~ 우리가 물을 휘젓는다'로 이어진다. 따라서 ④가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장이 없으면 'After all(결국)'로 시작하는 마지막 문장이 받을 주장이 사라진다.

passage: The world is interconnected and never stops changing, even when our senses miss the motion.
As you read, you are aging a little and your brain's neural networks are quietly rearranging.
Heraclitus said no one steps into the same river twice, for neither the river nor the person stays the same.
Cratylus added that we are not mere passive observers of the flow.
The instant we step in, we stir the water itself.
So we are agents of change, helping to shape the very world we move through.
summary.summary_template: Because the world and we ourselves are constantly __(A)__, we cannot be mere onlookers; the moment we step into the river we __(B)__ it and so help shape the change.
summary.explanation_ko: 세계와 우리는 끊임없이 (A)changing(변하)므로 구경꾼일 수 없고, 강에 들어서면 우리가 그것을 (B)alter(바꾸어) 변화를 빚는다. ②.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 changing, (B)는 alter여야 한다. preserve/ignore/watch 등은 능동적 변화라는 흐름과 반대이다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.answer: We are not mere passive observers.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 We + be동사 are + not + mere passive observers.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 어느 누구도 같은 강에 두 번 발을 들이지 못한다.
writing.answer: No one ever steps into the same river twice.
writing.explanation_ko: 부정 주어 No one + 부사 ever + 동사 steps into + the same river twice.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리가 강에 발을 들이는 순간, 우리는 그것을 휘저어 바꾼다.
conditions: we 를 주어로 두 번 사용할 것
writing.answer: The moment we step into the river, we stir it.
writing.explanation_ko: The moment(~하는 순간) + 주절 we stir it. step into(발을 들이다), stir(휘젓다).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Cratylus insisted that we are not mere passive ___________ of the flow, for stepping in changes the river.
writing.explanation_ko: 강을 바꾸는 능동적 주체와 대비되는 단어는 '관찰자(observers)'이다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Our world is not just interconnected, but ever-changing, even if we can't sense it.
writing.answer: 우리의 세계는 단지 서로 연결되어 있을 뿐만 아니라, 우리가 그것을 감지하지 못하더라도 끊임없이 변하고 있다.
writing.explanation_ko: not just A but B(단지 A뿐만 아니라 B), ever-changing(끊임없이 변하는), even if(비록 ~일지라도).
